questions.q: In the formula 'Total Sales = SUM(Sales[SalesAmount])', what does the equals sign mark?
options: The start of the formula
The end of the formula
A comparison between two values
The name of the function being used
questions.explain: The equals sign always marks the beginning of a DAX formula, just as in Excel.

questions.q: What is a "fully qualified" column reference?
options: A column reference that includes its table name, like Sales[SalesAmount]
A column that has had its data type explicitly set
A column with no blank or null values
A column referenced inside a variable
questions.explain: Fully qualified means the table name precedes the column name in brackets — good practice even when referencing a column in the same table.

questions.q: How must a table name with spaces be written in a DAX formula?
options: Wrapped in single quotes, like 'Reseller Sales'[Amount]
Wrapped in square brackets, like [Reseller Sales][Amount]
With spaces replaced by underscores automatically
Table names with spaces aren't allowed in DAX
questions.explain: Table names containing spaces, reserved keywords, or disallowed characters must be enclosed in single quotation marks.

questions.q: Is DAX case-sensitive once data is loaded into the model?
options: No — sum and SUM work identically, though capitals are the convention
Yes — function names must always be typed in all caps
Only table names are case-sensitive
Only column names are case-sensitive
questions.explain: DAX and the underlying engine are case-insensitive once data is loaded, unlike Power Query, which is case-sensitive.

questions.q: What does the formula bar's suggestions/autocomplete feature help with?
options: Completing function names and showing what arguments they expect, reducing syntax errors
Automatically writing entire measures for you without any input
Formatting visuals in the report canvas
Merging queries in Power Query
questions.explain: Autocomplete offers function names, brief descriptions, and expected arguments as you type — the fastest way to avoid typos and learn new functions.
